html:
The Bulgars were Turkic-speaking, partly nomadic tribes of the steppe north of the Black Sea, known from the late 400s. On the map for 600 and 700 they hold the lands around the Sea of Azov; by 800 and 900 the name sits on the lower Danube.

Around 630 their leader Kubrat united them in what Byzantine writers called Old Great Bulgaria. After his death the Khazars pushed in and the tribes split. One group went north to the Volga and founded Volga Bulgaria. Another, under Asparuh, moved west, beat a Byzantine army and in 681 settled south of the Danube.

That second state became the Bulgarian Empire. Its Bulgar rulers were a small elite over a large Slavic population, and they slowly merged with them. After the conversion to Christianity in 864 the Bulgars spoke Slavic, and only their name lives on in modern Bulgaria.
